A2_Scope.description: This chapter defines the axiomatic and operational structure of the probability function in the Behavioral Change Model (BCM 2.0/BEATRIX). It specifies the calculation, meaning, and modulation of probabilities as a core element of behavioral change architecture, simulation, and intervention planning. The module is mandatory for all BCM/BEATRIX applications modeling decision, transition, or effect chances.

goals: Formalization and operationalization of decision and transition probabilities in behavioral change
Integration of utility, willingness, awareness, context, and segment logic into probabilistic models
Enabling empirically testable, transparently documented, and auditable probability computations

A4_Axioms.name: Probabilistic Decision Architecture
A4_Axioms.definition: Any behavioral change is representable via probability functions between states/phases.
A4_Axioms.formal: P(i→j, t) = f(N(t), W(t), A_mod(t), S(t), C(t))

A4_Axioms.name: Utility Dependence
A4_Axioms.definition: Transition probability increases with subjectively perceived total utility.

A4_Axioms.name: Willingness as Switching Condition
A4_Axioms.definition: If willingness is not given, the probability of behavioral change is zero.

A4_Axioms.name: Awareness as Trigger
A4_Axioms.definition: Situationally activated awareness increases transition probability.

A4_Axioms.name: Context Dependence
A4_Axioms.definition: Context factors modulate all transition probabilities.

A4_Axioms.name: Segment Differentiation
A4_Axioms.definition: Each segment has its own probability functions and parameters.

A4_Axioms.name: Dynamics and Feedback
A4_Axioms.definition: Probabilities are time-dependent and are adapted through experience, feedback, and learning processes.
A4_Axioms.formal: P(i→j, t+1) = f(P(i→j, t), Feedback(t), Learning(t))

A4_Axioms.name: Social Reinforcement
A4_Axioms.definition: Social norms and observed behavior influence probabilities.

A4_Axioms.name: Uncertainty, Risk, and Ambiguity
A4_Axioms.definition: Higher uncertainty, perceived risk, or ambiguity reduce transition probabilities.

A4_Axioms.name: Measurability and Operationalization
A4_Axioms.definition: Probabilities must be empirically measurable and testable via observable transitions, repetitions, or experimental designs.

requirements: Loaded modules for utilities (BCM2_01_INU, BCM2_02_KNU, BCM2_03_IDN), awareness (BCM2_05_AWX), willingness (BCM2_06_KOM), segment logic (BCM2_08_PRB / BCM2_09_SEG), behavioral change journey (BCM2_10_JNY)
Context vector defined for each application

integration: Direct coupling to utility, willingness, awareness, segment, and context modules
Integrated in all agent-based simulations, policy and intervention architectures
Foundation for calibration of experimental and real-world behavioral models

constraints: Only BCM-conform terminology (no psychological, suggestive, or system-external terms)
No use for individual diagnostics; only for model-based analysis and simulation

literature: Theoretical and empirical work on probabilistic decision theory

A10_License_and_Usage.license: Use restricted to the BEATRIX/BCM 2.0 architecture with explicit initialization and inclusion of all mandatory modules.
conditions: All mandatory modules must be integrated
Commercial and scientific use requires written permission from FehrAdvice & Partners AG

summary: Formally transparent, traceable modeling and simulation of behavioral transitions
Integration of all relevant utility, willingness, awareness, segment, and context factors
Empirical testability, auditability, and governance for decision and intervention architectures in BCM 2.0/BEATRIX

Appendix.archived_content_notice: Earlier versions may exist for documentation/comparison only and must not be used for modeling, simulation, or interventions; only the current version (v2.0, July 2025) is applicable.

legacy_table_mapping.note: Legacy emphasizes monotonic dependence on W; current axiom defines W as a hard switch/zero condition under threshold.
Legacy logistic form is a specific functional instantiation of threshold sensitivity; current axiom stays abstract.
Segment-specific thresholds/parameters are covered by segment differentiation.
Journey-phase sensitivity can be represented as part of context/structural modulators; if modeled explicitly, it is included via C(t) or as a dedicated factor in f.
Asymptotic behavior supports probabilistic (non-deterministic) interpretation; measurability requirement remains.
Time-dynamics are explicitly captured via feedback/learning update.
Interventions affect probabilities via upstream inputs (utilities, awareness, willingness, context); represented by f(.) arguments.
Combined effect of BCM components is captured in the core functional dependency statement.
Experience learning changing slope/parameters is captured by probability update with learning/feedback.
Stochastic noise / non-determinism is consistent with empirical measurability and probabilistic interpretation.
